summary_for_children: Al-Qiyamah means The Resurrection. It says Allah can restore even our fingertips and teaches not to hurry when reciting.
environment_concept: A pattern of fingertip whorls in light on a stone (75:4).
architecture_and_scenery: Abstract sculpture of a hand made of light (no person), and a gentle path.

activities.name: Fingerprint
activities.description: Find four glowing whorls around the stone.
activities.label: artistic educational adaptation, not an event in the Quran

activities.name: Do not rush
activities.label: artistic educational adaptation, not an event in the Quran

status.playable_environment: first version built: a composed world (fingerprint, stones) with 1 hands-on activity in the scene
status.testing: not tested yet: written and type-checked, not yet checked on screen

depiction_rules: No prophet, person or representation of Allah is shown. Unseen realities are never pictured. Interactive activities are labelled as adaptations.

unique_world.visual_theme: A sunny yard behind a potter’s workshop with clay tablets drying on low stands and an ink card of your own prints on the bench

primary_mechanic.text: Six clay tablets each carry a fingerprint (loop, whorl or arch, with a small mark in one of four places); compare each with your own five prints and name the finger that made it, or say it is someone else’s (75:3-4, even the fingertips; 75:14-15, a witness against oneself). A wrong answer says whether the pattern or the mark differs.

unique_world.narrative_structure: A reading by the olives, the tablets in the yard, then a reading by the workshop
environment_behaviour: each tablet changes colour once read
unique_world.learning_objective: Know that Allah is able to put together even our fingertips, and that each person will witness against themselves (75:4, 75:14)

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: The Day of Resurrection
story_library.children_narration: Surah Al-Qiyamah reminds us that life is meaningful and that we will return to Allah. It invites people to reflect on their choices and consider the life to come. It also reminds us of Allah's power to create and resurrect.

world_idea.title: The Hall of Reflection
world_idea.description: Explore symbolic architecture built around time, memory, and responsibility. Do not portray the actual Day of Resurrection.

story_library.checks: Every reference exists in the verified text (checked 2026-11-04). Narration is draft, written by the owner, not reviewed by a scholar.
